expected.title: Approximate versus exact L2 controllability for canonical complex two-state scalar-input difference systems with two irrationally related delays
expected.author: Yacine Chitour; Guilherme Mazanti; Mario Sigalotti
expected.difficulty_reason: The endpoint adjoint reduces to a weighted irrational-rotation operator. Its kernel is characterized by exponential twisting and Fourier uniqueness; exact observability follows from rational-delay Toeplitz inverses with a size-independent bound, while dense eigenvalues approaching zero obstruct exact control.

e0\). The state history space is \(L^2((-1,0),\mathbb C^2)\), with scalar complex input. The approximate-control assertion is \(T\ge2\) and \(0
otin\mathcal S\); the exact-control assertion is \(T\ge2\) and \(0
otin\overline{\mathcal S}\), where \(\mathcal S\) is the set of all complex values of \( eta+\alpha^{1-L}\). Adjacent article results and background are preserved as author context, and are not additional selected problems. The generic complex-vector normal-form claim is not part of this item.
